Package com.phasmidsoftware.gryphon.java

Class MinimumSpanningTree

java.lang.Object
com.phasmidsoftware.gryphon.java.MinimumSpanningTree
public class MinimumSpanningTree extends Object
Java façade for minimum spanning tree algorithms on weighted undirected graphs.

All methods operate on a WeightedGraph<V, E> whose edges carry an attribute of type E. The edge attribute is used directly as the priority key — no separate weight extractor is needed.

Both algorithms require an undirected graph. Calling either on a directed graph throws IllegalStateException.

Prim result: Map<V, WeightedEdge<V, E>> mapping each non-source vertex to its cheapest MST edge. The start vertex is absent.

Kruskal result: List<WeightedEdge<V, E>> in non-decreasing order according to the supplied comparator.

Option 1 example (Double weights): 


 WeightedGraph<Integer, Double> g = WeightedGraph.undirected();
 g.addEdge(new WeightedEdge<>(0, 1, 0.26));
 g.addEdge(new WeightedEdge<>(0, 7, 0.16));

 Map<Integer, WeightedEdge<Integer, Double>> mst = MinimumSpanningTree.prim(g, 0);
 double total = mst.values().stream().mapToDouble(WeightedEdge::attribute).sum();

Option 3 example (custom attribute type): 


 WeightedGraph<Building, TunnelProperties> g = WeightedGraph.undirected();
 g.addEdge(new WeightedEdge<>(b1, b2, tunnelProperties));

 Map<Building, WeightedEdge<Building, TunnelProperties>> mst =
     MinimumSpanningTree.prim(g, start, Comparator.comparingInt(tp -> tp.cost));

 mst.forEach((b, e) -> System.out.println(b + ": cost=" + e.attribute().cost
                                           + " length=" + e.attribute().length));

      Runs Prim's algorithm on a graph whose edges carry Double weights.

      Parameters:

      start - the source vertex (absent from the result).
